answer.rationale: Competitor price cut is creating immediate churn pressure on price-sensitive SMB segment. memory_73 confirms targeted promotional pricing is effective for this exact segment with strong acquisition and revenue lift. memory_31 shows signup simplification works for SMB activation but doesn't directly address price objections. memory_91 and memory_86 improve engagement and adoption but won't retain accounts actively considering competitor offerings. A small_guarded_test of promotional pricing on at-risk SMB cohorts lets us defend revenue while containing discount scope and learning elasticity. This preserves the option to layer in activation messaging (memory_91) or onboarding improvements (memory_86) later. Risk: deep discounting can erode long-term pricing power and LTV if not bounded; escalation to enterprise_sales_assist is available for strategic accounts. The urgency of doubled churn conversations justifies faster-than-standard deployment, but guarding scope preserves ability to reverse if discount proves unsustainable.
